stories.head: Contentstack Launches Canoe: AI Visibility Tool Showing Brands What AI Tells Buyers
stories.plain: Contentstack's first standalone product, priced at $279/month, audits how a brand appears inside AI-generated answers, benchmarks it against up to ten rivals, and outputs a ranked fix list that AI agents can act on. This is a concrete, purchasable GEO tool — the clearest signal yet that AI-answer visibility is becoming a standard martech budget line.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Launches Agent Teams After Acquiring DoubleO.ai to Run Full GTM Plays Autonomously
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and is shipping Agent Teams: coordinated AI agents that execute complete go-to-market motions — from detecting a buying signal to taking action — without human babysitting. This raises the stakes for how agentic AI is bought into sales and marketing stacks, and puts pressure on standalone GTM point solutions.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Entirely Different 'AI Shelves,' Disrupting Brand and Price Hierarchies
stories.plain: Jellyfish research shows that AI shopping assistants recommend products in a completely different order than traditional search results, reshuffling competitive dynamics and price positioning. The firm is launching a 'Share of Model' measurement product. Marketers who ignore AI shelf placement risk losing buyers before a human ever sees a listing.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust Ecosystem to Verify AI Agent Intent Throughout Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: DataDome now adds real-time behavioral checks to Experian's Agent Trust platform, verifying not just who an AI agent represents but whether its actions stay within authorized boundaries during a transaction. This is an early-market answer to a pressing governance question: how do you police what autonomous agents do after they're launched?

stories.head: Mixpanel Introduces Agent Intelligence to Connect AI Agent Conversations to Business Outcomes
stories.plain: Mixpanel's new Agent Intelligence layer links what an AI agent says to downstream customer behavior and revenue metrics, giving product and marketing teams a way to measure whether their agents actually work. As agentic deployments multiply, the ability to tie agent conversations to business outcomes is becoming a critical buying criterion.

stories.head: Contentstack Launches Canoe: AI Visibility Tool Showing Brands What AI Tells Buyers
stories.plain: Contentstack's Contentstack Canoe is a standalone $279/month product that audits how a brand appears in AI search answers, benchmarks it against up to ten rivals, and produces a ranked fix list that AI agents can act on. It's one of the first commercial tools purpose-built for Generative Engine Optimization, making GEO measurable for everyday marketing teams.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Launches Agent Teams After Acquiring DoubleO.ai to Run Full GTM Plays Autonomously
stories.plain: ZoomInfo acquired DoubleO.ai and used it to ship Agent Teams, a system that coordinates multiple AI agents across a company's tools, signals, and ZoomInfo data to execute complete go-to-market motions from signal to action without human babysitting. This raises the bar for agentic decisioning in B2B marketing and sets a precedent for acqui-hire-powered agent stacks.

stories.head: Braze Expands AI from Content Creation into Campaign Operations and External LLM Connections
stories.plain: Braze added AI decisioning tools that automate campaign health checks and let marketers connect the platform to external LLMs like Claude. This moves Braze from AI-assisted copywriting into operational AI, meaning the platform itself starts making or validating decisions — a shift that changes how enterprise buyers evaluate and govern CEPs.

stories.head: Jellyfish Research: AI Shopping Assistants Create Radically Different 'AI Shelves,' Reshaping Brand Competition
stories.plain: Jellyfish's research shows that AI shopping assistants build their own product shortlists that bear little resemblance to traditional search rankings, upending price positioning and brand leadership. Jellyfish is launching a 'Share of Model' measurement product in response. This is hard evidence that GEO now directly affects revenue, not just traffic.

stories.head: DataDome Joins Experian Agent Trust Ecosystem to Verify AI Agent Intent Throughout Agentic Commerce
stories.plain: Experian's Agent Trust platform now includes DataDome, which continuously checks whether an AI agent's actions match what it was actually authorized to do — not just who it represents at login. As agentic commerce grows, this kind of runtime governance is essential infrastructure for brands that let AI agents make purchases or commitments on behalf of customers.

themes.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Discoverability Rules
body: Brands are waking up to a new reality: AI assistants and generative engines are becoming primary gatekeepers of purchase decisions, and the old SEO playbook does not transfer cleanly. New tooling like Contentstack Canoe is emerging specifically to show marketers what AI models are actually saying about their brand to buyers — a category that did not exist 18 months ago.

The implications run deep. Jellyfish research shows AI shopping is upending price positioning and brand leadership in ways that favour well-structured, authoritative content over paid-search dominance. Optimising for generative engine models requires rethinking not just keywords but the entire evidence trail an AI summariser can draw on.

themes.head: Agentic AI Enters the GTM Stack
body: AI agents are moving from demos to live commercial workflows, and the governance gap is already visible. ZoomInfo's acquisition of DoubleO.ai to launch Agent Teams, Mixpanel's Agent Intelligence, and Experian's Agent Trust ecosystem all signal that orchestrating and auditing agents is now a first-order operational problem for revenue teams.

The risk is real: GTM teams report losing track of what their agents are doing, which decisions they are making, and whether those decisions align with brand or compliance intent. DataDome's move to add continuous intent verification to agentic commerce underlines that trust infrastructure must be built in parallel with agent deployment, not retrofitted later.

themes.head: Speed vs. Quality: AI Made Marketing Faster, Not Better
body: A mounting body of practitioner evidence — and frank editorial — argues that the first wave of AI adoption turbocharged output volume while quietly eroding creative distinctiveness and strategic rigour. Mixbook's deliberate choice to keep AI entirely out of its customer-facing messaging is a telling counter-signal: consumers increasingly associate AI-labelled content with cheapness rather than innovation.

Job-posting data reinforces the tension: employers want AI-fluent marketers, but the skills most in demand are judgment, editing, and quality control — precisely the human layer that prevents AI-generated work from being fast-but-forgettable. The strategic decision for 2026 is not whether to use AI but how to use it without losing the brand voice that earns long-term loyalty.

themes.head: CRM & Data Platforms Evolve Into Pipeline Action Engines
body: The centre of gravity in martech is shifting from data warehousing to real-time activation. Salesforce's acquisition of Listen Labs to embed AI-powered customer research, Growth7's platform that converts CRM records directly into pipeline actions, and Braze's expansion from content generation into full campaign operations all point to the same structural change: the CRM is becoming a decision engine, not a record-keeper.

This collapse of the insight-to-action gap has significant workforce implications. When platforms autonomously surface intent signals and trigger personalised sequences, the marketer's job shifts toward strategy, oversight, and exception-handling rather than execution — redefining what 'operating a CRM' even means for teams entering 2027 planning.
ev: MarTech · Braze expands AI to campaign operations

themes.head: Trust, Regulation & AI Governance As Competitive Moat
body: Regulatory pressure on digital marketing is accelerating from multiple directions simultaneously. US states are legislating social-media access and data use, identity fraud is growing more adaptive according to Persona's research, and IBM's launch of a self-hosted deployment for enterprise AI signals that data sovereignty is now a buying criterion, not just a compliance checkbox.

For CMOs, governance is transitioning from a legal department concern to a brand & competitive differentiator. Vendors that can demonstrate transparent supply chains (Jamloop's Verified Supply for CTV), verified agent intent, and sovereign AI deployment are gaining procurement preference — meaning trust architecture is now part of the martech selection conversation alongside features and price.
ev: MarTech · states rewriting social media rules

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack, the real contest is no longer about adopting AI but about governing it well enough to earn buyer trust at the moment AI itself has become the buyer's first advisor.
